english.notes:
Notes
(i) Schedule 2 to the Regulations makes provision for the various notices that can be served. These are an information notice, enforcement notice and prohibition notice.
(ii) As per paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 2, any persons served with enforcement or a prohibition notice may be able to appeal to the relevant body in England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland.
(iii) As per paragraph 3(2) of Schedule 2, an enforcement or prohibition notice must detail the right of appeal and any period in which an appeal may be brought.
(iv) As per paragraph 3(3) of Schedule 2, the period within which an appeal may be brought is 28 days or, in the case of an enforcement notice, the period specified in the notice, whichever ends earlier.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
